title: Grade 4 French — Wed, Jun 11
description: Les aliments — Day 3 of 5: Meals and drinks
subject: french

questions.question: How do you say 'breakfast' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Le petit-déjeuner' = breakfast. 'Je mange le petit-déjeuner à sept heures.' = I eat breakfast at seven o'clock.

questions.question: How do you say 'lunch' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Le déjeuner' = lunch. 'Je mange le déjeuner à midi.' = I eat lunch at noon.

questions.question: How do you say 'dinner' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Le dîner' = dinner. 'Je mange le dîner à sept heures du soir.' = I eat dinner at seven in the evening.

questions.question: What is 'le goûter' in English?
questions.explanation: 'Le goûter' = afternoon snack (typically for children, around 4 pm). Very common in France! 'Je mange le goûter après l'école.' = I have a snack after school.

questions.question: How do you say 'water' in French?
questions.explanation: 'L'eau' = water (feminine, so 'l'' before 'e'). 'Je bois de l'eau.' = I drink water.

questions.question: How do you say 'milk' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Le lait' = milk. 'Je bois du lait au petit-déjeuner.' = I drink milk at breakfast.

questions.question: How do you say 'juice' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Le jus de fruit' = fruit juice. 'Je bois du jus d'orange.' = I drink orange juice.

questions.question: What verb means 'to drink' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Boire' = to drink. 'Je bois' (I drink), 'tu bois' (you drink), 'il/elle boit' (he/she drinks).

questions.question: Complete: 'Je ___ du pain au petit-déjeuner.' (I eat bread at breakfast.)
questions.explanation: 'Je mange du pain.' = I eat bread. 'Manger' = to eat. 'Du pain' = some bread (partitive article).

questions.question: How do you say 'I drink orange juice' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Je bois du jus d'orange.' = I drink orange juice. 'Boire' → 'je bois'. 'Du jus d'orange' = some orange juice.

questions.question: What do French children typically eat for 'le goûter' (afternoon snack)?
options: Pain au chocolat or a tartine (bread with butter/jam)
questions.explanation: French children often eat 'pain au chocolat' (chocolate croissant) or a 'tartine' (bread with butter and jam) for le goûter. It is a beloved French tradition.

questions.question: Translate: 'For lunch, I eat rice and vegetables.'
options: Au dîner, je bois du riz et des légumes.
Au déjeuner, je mange du riz et des légumes.
Au petit-déjeuner, je mange du riz et des légumes.
Au goûter, je mange du riz.
questions.explanation: 'Au déjeuner, je mange du riz et des légumes.' = For lunch, I eat rice and vegetables. 'Au déjeuner' = for/at lunch.

questions.question: How many meals (repas) do French people typically have per day?
options: One large meal in the evening
questions.explanation: Three main meals: petit-déjeuner (breakfast), déjeuner (lunch), dîner (dinner). 'Le goûter' is an extra snack for children.

questions.question: How do you say 'What do you eat for breakfast?' in French?
options: Qu'est-ce que tu manges au dîner?
Qu'est-ce que tu manges au petit-déjeuner?
Qu'est-ce que tu bois au déjeuner?
Qu'est-ce que tu fais au matin?
questions.explanation: 'Qu'est-ce que tu manges au petit-déjeuner?' = What do you eat for breakfast? 'Qu'est-ce que' = what; 'tu manges' = you eat.

questions.question: Match the meal to the French word: morning meal / midday meal / evening meal:
questions.explanation: petit-déjeuner (morning) → déjeuner (midday) → dîner (evening). This is the standard French daily meal order.
